subject: English
summaryPoints: Subject-verb agreement requires finite verbs to match their grammatical subjects in person and number; compound subjects joined by 'and' take plural verbs, but subjects linked by correlatives ('either...or', 'neither...nor') agree with the closer subject.
Parenthetical expressions introduced by 'as well as', 'together with', 'like', and 'in addition to' do not compound the grammatical subject; the verb agrees strictly with the original head noun.
Indefinite pronouns such as 'everybody', 'everyone', 'nobody', 'each', and 'either' take singular verbs in standard formal English.

Exceptions to tense backshifting in reported speech occur when: (1) reporting general scientific truths or permanent facts, (2) the reporting verb is in the present tense, (3) the statement contains modals like would/could/should/might, or (4) the statement follows 'wish', 'would rather', or 'had better'.

The subjunctive verb 'wish' expresses dissatisfaction or desire for change: wish + simple past denotes present unreality, wish + past perfect denotes past regret, and wish + would expresses dissatisfaction with another's behavior.

A formal job application letter comprises six standard components: applicant heading, date, employer inside address, salutation, body paragraphs (opening interest, qualifications/experience, personal traits, appreciation), complimentary close ('Sincerely'), and signature.

formulas.label: Correlative Conjunction Agreement (Proximity Rule)
formulas.expr: Either S1 or S2 + Verb(agrees with S2)  |  Neither S1 nor S2 + Verb(agrees with S2)

formulas.label: Intervening Parenthetical Subject Agreement
formulas.expr: Head Noun(singular) + as well as / together with / like + Noun(plural) + Verb(singular)

formulas.label: Subjunctive Wish + Would Formula
formulas.expr: Subject + wish + Subject(different) + would + V1(bare infinitive)  [Expresses: complaint / demand to change]

formulas.label: No-Backshift Reported Speech Condition
formulas.expr: Reporting Verb (present/says) + that + Reported Clause (no tense backshift)  OR  Reporting permanent universal fact

examTip: A major EUEE subject-verb agreement trap is the phrase 'as well as' or 'along with': 'The manager, as well as the workers, is (NOT are) responsible.' The verb agrees strictly with 'manager'. Also, remember that in reported speech, universal truths do not backshift: 'The teacher said that water boils at 100°C' (NOT boiled).

keyDefinitions.definition: The grammatical rule stipulating that a finite verb must match its subject in both number (singular/plural) and person (first, second, third).
The agreement principle dictating that when subjects are connected by 'either...or' or 'neither...nor', the finite verb agrees with the closer subject constituent.
A formal business document submitted to an employer highlighting an applicant's qualifications, professional experience, and motivation for a posted position.
A behavioral approach adopted by parties in a dispute, categorized into avoidance (flight), competition/domination (fight), and collaborative win-win problem-solving.

eueeFocusTopics: Subject-verb agreement: correlative conjunctions ('neither...nor') and parenthetical phrases ('as well as')
Agreement with indefinite pronouns ('everybody', 'each' take singular verbs)
Exceptions to tense backshifting in reported speech (scientific facts, present reporting verbs)
Subjunctive 'wish' patterns (wish + past simple vs past perfect vs would)
Standard conventions, layout, and salutations of formal job application letters
